about.title: San Carlos Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A defective product doesn't announce itself before it fails — a power tool that shorts out, a car part that snaps, a kitchen appliance that overheats. In San Carlos, people encounter these products at home along tree-lined streets near San Carlos Avenue, at work, and in vehicles traveling El Camino Real or US-101 daily. California law leans on strict liability for these cases, which means the focus stays on whether the product was defective and caused harm, not on proving someone was careless. That distinction matters, because it can simplify what's otherwise a complicated fight against manufacturers with more resources and legal teams than an individual has. We handle product liability claims on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless money is recovered. If a defective product hurt you in San Carlos, holding onto it and reaching out early can make a real difference in how the claim unfolds.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters for San Carlos Residents

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California's strict liability rules, the case usually centers on the defect and the harm it caused, not on digging up proof that a manufacturer was careless.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even the retailer who sold the product in San Carlos may all be part of the claim, which can widen where compensation comes from.

items.title: Preserving the Product Protects Your Case
items.desc: Keeping the defective item intact — rather than discarding or repairing it — gives our team the physical evidence needed to build a strict liability claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California's strict liability standard generally lets you focus on showing the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This is often more direct than trying to prove carelessness on the manufacturer's part.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Keep it exactly as it was at the time of the incident, if it's safe to do so. Don't attempt repairs or throw it away — the product itself is often the most important piece of evidence in a defect claim.

items.question: Is there a cost to have our team review my case in San Carlos?
items.answer: No. We offer free case reviews, and we typically work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
